name: SIGMA - Password Spray Indicator via Failed Logons From a Single Source (Windows Security 4625) [threshold]
description: Elastic threshold companion for rules/sigma/auth_win_bruteforce_source_spray.yml (issue #192, added from a security-auditor review finding: the per-account threshold on 4625 alone misses a password spray, where few passwords are tried against many accounts so no single account's failure count crosses the per-account threshold). Buckets Security 4625 failed logons by source IP (winlog.event_data.IpAddress) and alerts when a single source touches >=6 distinct target accounts (winlog.event_data.TargetUserName cardinality) within a 5-minute window. The Sigma file is the documented logic-of-record; this threshold rule adds the cardinality count that sigma_eval.py / the lucene conversion target cannot express. Query excludes the same 4 sentinel values #342 established for the source.ip ECS copy (issue #370, live-verified against a real Elasticsearch query_string search: the issue's own suggested fix only excluded 3 of the 4 - "" (empty string) is a genuinely distinct, separately-emitted sentinel value from "-", not covered by excluding "-" alone) - without this, every local/console/service-account 4625 (no real network source) collapses into one bucket, and 6 distinct accounts failing a local logon within the window fires a severity:high alert with no real attacking source IP. Known limitation (security-auditor finding, #370 review): excluding these 4 sentinels also removes the only coverage this rule accidentally had for a genuine ON-HOST password spray (e.g. runas/LogonUser() from an already-landed foothold, which logs 4625 with IpAddress:"-" too) - that population is no longer bucketed by anything. Deliberately accepted: the excluded traffic was overwhelmingly false-positive noise (this issue's own premise), and a correct fix for the local-spray case needs a SEPARATE companion rule bucketing on winlog.computer_name instead of IpAddress, not a weaker exclusion here - tracked as a new follow-up, deliberately out of scope for this fix. security-auditor review (#393): this rule's "from": "now-6m" / "interval": "5m" had the same undocumented flat +1-minute-overlap shape as its sibling threshold rules, with the identical mathematical gap - a real sliding 5-minute window is fully contained in a single 6-minute run window only 20% of the time for an arbitrary-phase campaign. Corrected to "from": "now-10m" (lookback >= interval + the 5-minute detection window), which GUARANTEES full containment. Cost: the effective counting window widens from 6 to 10 minutes and duplicate-alert risk across overlapping runs is not independently verified against multiple real Kibana scheduled runs.
author: Suburban-SOC
false_positives: A misconfigured application or service account retrying the same stale credential against many resources from one host.
NAT/proxy gateways where many real users' failed logons share one apparent source IP.
